slides.title: riskdep: DeFi risk dependencies
slides.subtitle: How the project works · DeFi Risk Dependency Challenge, Belem Capital, EPFL Hackathon 2026
slides.notes: Sources: README.md, docs/analysis/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/hackaton_instruction/GOAL.md, CLAUDE.md. riskdep is a Python CLI (python3 -m riskdep) with an HTTP API and a React web UI.

slides.title: The question we answer
bullets: A dependency of a position is hit
How much is lost?
How fast does it land?
Stay or exit, given what exiting costs?
Judged on: discovery 30 %, impact 30 %
decision usefulness 25 %, working demo on real data 15 %
slides.notes: The brief's worked trade-off: a book in ten 10 % pockets, one is hit, unwinding costs 11 %: exiting is certain and costly, staying is cheap and uncertain.

slides.title: Five modes, one command
table: the dependency graph, siblings, oracle classes
what each market and depositor loses when a node fails
loss, timing and STAY / REDUCE / EXIT
slides.notes: analyze estimates a risk; the two watch modes detect events; graph draws dependencies; shock propagates a failure through them. All read the same sources through the same modules.

slides.title: The pipeline
bullets: Discover: from one address to everything it depends on
Price the risk: probabilities per layer, or a known incident
Propagate: the shock engine, market by market
Decide: verdict given the incident, breakeven p*
Watch: detect it live, alert the depositor
slides.notes: Steps 1–4 answer 'how much and should I leave'; step 5 answers 'when' in real time. The fork demo plays all five on a real vault.

slides.title: 1. Dependency discovery
bullets: Vault → adapters → Morpho Blue markets → oracles → feeds
Who controls each contract: proxy admins, owners, timelocks
Issuers and their backing (registry, Pharos)
Sibling markets sharing a collateral, asset or price input
Oracle class: price-tracking or constant-price
slides.notes: graph.py, siblings.py, oracle_class.py, admin.py. The chain decides, the APIs find: the Morpho API lists positions and vaults, every amount is then read on-chain. Example: graph --vault 0xE018…1965 --replay (RockawayX USDC Yield).

slides.title: 2–3. Impact: two engines
left: A failure on a node of the graph
Edge rules carry it to the next node
right: A probability per layer, per year
slides.notes: engine.py (pure) with rules in registry.json (engine) or a --rules file; simulate.py and propagate.py. Probabilities: exploit priors from DefiLlama's hack record by size band, category and age; market events from registry.json; see the probabilities deck.

slides.title: 4. Decision
bullets: Verdict given the incident: EXIT or STAY, and why
Breakeven p*: how likely must it be for leaving to pay
Cost of leaving (yield given up, or an exit cost) ÷ loss saved
A book of vaults: act first on the lowest p*
Outside view: Nexus cover prices, shown, never used
slides.notes: Brief's example, examples/brief-ten-pockets.json, mGLOeuro -30 %, 11 % exit cost: 'Leaving Belem RWA EURCV costs 110,000 USD for sure, against 53,445 saved if the incident comes: stay.' f(x) vault, fxSAVE -30 %: EXIT, it pays above a 7.92 % probability over 30 days.

slides.title: 5. Monitoring: watch
bullets: Polls every block (12 s), 2 blocks behind the head
Alerts: info, warn, critical, in the terminal and JSON
Bad debt, oracle moves, liquidations, utilisation
Upgrades, owners, feeds, timelock queues, mints
Cursor saved last: a restart misses no block
Cross-checks: a second RPC, the API against the chain
slides.notes: watch.py, rules.py, market_risk.py, drain.py, exit_queue.py, admin.py. What each alert means and what to do: docs/reference/alert-runbook.md. Thresholds in registry.json (watch).

slides.title: Data sources, all public
table: PT markets, implied yield, exit quotes
slides.notes: Trust model: the chain is authoritative; APIs only find things. A second RPC (dRPC) checks block hashes; the Morpho API is checked against the chain at 0.5 %. Endpoints and limits: docs/analysis/PROVIDERS.md.

slides.title: Is the number defensible?
slides.notes: riskdep backtest: reads the state 60 blocks before the real liquidations, applies the oracle's observed fall, compares with the 33 Liquidate events. Within 1 % where positions were fully liquidated. Not tested: the oracle's fall itself and the squeeze. The fork demo adds a second check: 251,761 predicted vs 252,914 observed.

graph, analyze --vault, analyze --book, watch --replay

Sponsor's vault (Belem RWA EURCV) and its curator's book

slides.title: Interfaces
slides.notes: uv run uvicorn riskdep.api:app --reload (docs at /docs). web/: React single-page app, one page per mode; runs with mocks copied from real CLI output when no backend.

slides.title: How it is built
bullets: Design first: plans in plan/, numbered decisions
Pure rules and engine, I/O at the edges
No literal thresholds: registry.json, each with a basis
One cached fetcher, one clock: any live run can be a test
288 tests, all offline; ruff in pre-commit and CI
slides.notes: Code comments cite plan decisions (D21, D182…). The cached fetcher keys every request; offline runs use the snapshot date as now (clock.py).

slides.title: Limits
bullets: Ethereum only; Solana, Base and other chains not read
Probabilities are base rates, layers mostly independent
analyze covers Pendle PT collateral on Morpho Blue
Free RPC: short state window, no backfill
Issuer data (NAV, reserves) taken as published
